parasite_note: Often carries "codworm" (a roundworm larva) in its flesh. Seals are the worm's final host, so codworm is more common where seal numbers have recovered.
food_safety: Cook to 145°F, or freeze before eating raw or lightly cured.
source: NOAA Fisheries; FDA Fish and Fishery Products Hazards and Controls Guidance

parasite_note: Like many Pacific rockfish, can carry Anisakis roundworm larvae. Whales, dolphins, and seals are the worm's final hosts.
food_safety: Cook to 145°F, or freeze before eating raw.
source: FDA Fish and Fishery Products Hazards and Controls Guidance

parasite_note: Anglers often find "spaghetti worms" (tapeworm larvae) in the flesh, especially in warmer months. They do not infect people.
food_safety: Safe to eat when cooked. Cut out any worms you see.

parasite_note: Larger fish often have "spaghetti worms" (tapeworm larvae) in the flesh. They do not infect people.
food_safety: Safe to eat when cooked. Cut out any worms you see.
